entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since ~July 18, 2026):

---

- 
**GRPM Grand River Adventure, Aug. 15, 2026:** The Grand Rapids Public Museum held its 4th annual Grand River Adventure on August 15, a full-day open-house event celebrating the history, science, culture, art, and stewardship of the Grand River Watershed.
 
The event explored community organizations working on riverfront projects and what is actively happening along the Grand River.
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum / Grand Rapids Magazine, Aug. 13, 2026)

- 
**GRPM "Old Streets" Exhibit Expansion, open as of May 2026:** The Grand Rapids Public Museum opened a second floor of its "Streets of Old Grand Rapids" exhibit, featuring additional artifacts and former businesses from the 1890s, with the main attraction being the Kent Scientific Institute, the original institution that became the GRPM.
 (WGRD, May 5, 2026) *(Flagged here as potentially not yet captured in the Aug. 1 base research.)*

- 
**H.R. 3255 federal recognition bill stalled, as of Aug. 10, 2026:** H.R. 3255, the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act of 2025, remained referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources with no scheduled hearing as of August 10, 2026.
 
The companion Senate Bill 2160, introduced June 25, 2025 by Sen. Gary Peters, also remained in the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs with no scheduled hearing.
 (Cherokee One Feather, Aug. 10, 2026)

- 
**New book published Jan. 13, 2026:** "The Historical Archaeology of Michigan" by Dean L. Anderson, Michael S. Nassaney, and Krysta Ryzewski was published January 13, 2026 by the University Press of Florida (276 pages, ISBN 978-0813079455), covering 400 years of Michigan archaeology including Anishinaabe peoples, the fur trade, and settler colonialism.
 (University Press of Florida / Amazon, 2026) *(Included as likely post-cutoff for the base research.)*

- 
**Grand River Bands 44th annual Homecoming, June 13-14, 2026:** The Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians hosted the 44th annual Homecoming of the Three Fires at Riverside Park in Grand Rapids, offering two days of traditional Native American culture and community gathering.
 (Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians website, June 12, 2026)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days, plus a few close-in items from July 2026 that postdate the River Brain's August 1 base:

---

- **Michigan Transformational Brownfield Program reformed, July 22, 2026:** 
Gov. Whitmer signed Senate Bill 723 as Public Act 36 of 2026 on July 22, revising the state's Transformational Brownfield Program by expanding oversight, increasing transparency, tying reimbursements to measurable project performance, and raising incentive capacity for future projects.
 
The law roughly doubles annual capacity, authorizing an additional $80 million in state tax capture and raising the yearly ceiling to as much as $160 million, with the total aggregate cap rising to roughly $3.2 billion.
 
State officials specifically cited stalled riverfront work in Grand Rapids as an example of the capacity constraints the law is meant to relieve.
 (Environment+Energy Leader, ~July 25, 2026)

- **New TBP funding pipeline for Grand Rapids waterfront developments, July 14, 2026:** 
Major waterfront developments in Grand Rapids, Muskegon and Holland are positioned to benefit from the newly expanded Transformational Brownfield Program.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business, July 14, 2026)

- **East Riverfront Park groundbreaking, $19 million, August 21, 2025 (milestone now current):** 
City and state leaders broke ground on the East Riverfront project, a $19 million investment to turn an old industrial site into accessible green space, located just west of the Acrisure Amphitheater.
 
When it opens in 2026, it will serve as a vital connection in the 85-mile Grand River Greenway linking communities across Kent and Ottawa counties.
 (City of Grand Rapids, August 21, 2025)

- **Federal riverfront property in Creston lost to GSA auction, February 13, 2026:** 
Grand Rapids was unsuccessful in lowering the $4.5 million purchase price to acquire the former U.S. Naval and Marine Corps Reserve Center at 1863 Monroe Ave. NW from the GSA; the negotiated price proved too high after all development proposals found the project infeasible.
 
The GSA will now list the 3.5-acre riverfront property just south of Riverside Park for public purchase, with no known timeline.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business, February 13, 2026)

- **Parks department acquires 6 land bank lots for trails and green space, May 2026:** 
The Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation Department is making plans for trails and green space on six lots acquired from the land bank that were deemed unbuildable for housing.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business, May 11, 2026)

- **Brownfield plan amendment hearings for townhomes and industrial facility, July 2026:** 
Grand Rapids officials are considering brownfield plan incentives for two projects, one adding 20 townhomes at three city sites and another building a nearly 100,000-square-foot industrial facility, with public hearings scheduled for July 21 after both received preliminary Brownfield

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Now let me do a more targeted search for any Grand River-specific news from the past 30 days (mid-July to mid-August 2026), including the restoration project construction status.
Based on my searches, here is what is genuinely new or changed within roughly the last 30 days (mid-July to mid-August 2026). Note that most regulatory actions (DNR 2026 fishing regs, MDHHS Eat Safe Fish Guide, EGLE permit) date from April through June 2026 and fall outside the 30-day window. The most current actionable update is the dam removal construction launch. No new public health advisory, EGLE permit action, or Grand River-specific DNR fishing regulation change was found within the last 30 days.

---

- **Grand River dam removal construction began July 1, 2026:** 
In-river construction started July 1 to remove four low-head dams from just upstream of Bridge Street Bridge to the Fulton Street Bridge. The July 1 start date aligns with regulatory requirements designed to protect fish spawning periods and prevent invasive sea lampreys from moving past the Sixth Street Dam.
 (City of Grand Rapids)

- **Active construction season runs through mid-October or early November 2026:** 
Trucks and heavy equipment are moving rocks and boulders in and out of the flowing river channel throughout the construction season, which runs roughly July through mid-October or early November each year, weather and river conditions permitting.
 (Spectrum News)

- **Contractor and scope confirmed:** 
Over the coming weeks, the Taplin Group, the city's contractor for the lower reach project, will build causeways to allow construction equipment to safely travel in the river; a small cofferdam will also be built to isolate a section of Dam 2 to construct the boulder arch feature.
 (City of Grand Rapids)

- **Habitat enhancement scope:** 
Work will include installation of natural rock structures (boulder arches, riffles, emergent habitat boulders, and bank vanes) and enhancement of aquatic habitat across 2,887 feet and 30 acres of river corridor, with improved habitat targeted for lake sturgeon, river redhorse, and snuffbox mussel.
 (City of Grand Rapids)

- **MDHHS 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guide released June 8, 2026 (just outside 30-day window, flagged for reference):** 
The guide covers 696 bodies of water in Michigan; in 2026, MDHHS reported 59 guidelines were relaxed while 65 became more protective.
 No Grand River-specific advisory change was identified in search results. (WNEM / MDHHS)

- **No new public health advisory or EGLE permit action found for the Grand River in the last 30 days.** No E. coli or contact advisories specific to the Grand River in Kent County were found dated July or August 2026.

- **Grand River dam removal active, one month in (Aug. 3, 2026):** 
As of August 3, the Grand River Restoration project is actively drawing public attention near Ah-Nab-Awen Park, with crews removing a dam just north of Gillett Bridge, one of four low-head dams being removed between I-196 and Fulton Street in this first phase, expected to take about two years.
 
The project involves replacing the dams with natural rock structures, with crews currently working on the western half of the dam near Ah-Nab-Awen Park.
 (WZZM13 / Yahoo News, Aug. 3, 2026)

- **Return to the River Festival 2026 date confirmed: August 22-23 (announced prior to Aug. 17):** 
DGRI's Return to the River Instagram confirmed the festival dates as August 22 and 23, 2026, a free music and art festival in downtown Grand Rapids.
 
The festival takes place at multiple venues along the Grand River, including 555 Monroe Skate Park, Sixth Street Park, and the Sixth Street Bridge.
 (Return to the River Instagram / ExperienceGR, Aug. 2026)

- **GRPM Grand River Adventure held August 15, 2026:** 
The Grand Rapids Public Museum hosted its 4th annual Grand River Adventure on August 15, 2026, celebrating history, science, culture, art, and stewardship of the Grand River Watershed.
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum, Aug. 2026)

Construction began on a new three-quarter-mile segment of the Grand River Edges Trail between Leonard Street NW and Ann Street NW, which will eventually include street crossings, lighting, benches, and native plants.
 
This extension is part of the larger Grand River Greenway project, which will stretch 171 miles from Lake Michigan to Owosso when completed.
 
The Edges Trail segment is expected to be complete by end of 2026.
 (WOOD TV / WOOD Radio, June 15, 2026)

A new tunnel under Northland Drive near Blythefield Country Club in Plainfield Charter Township broke ground, removing what Kent County Parks Director Ben Swayze described as "one of the biggest barriers for people running, walking, and" using the Greenway corridor.
 
Construction on two sections of Ottawa County's Idema Explorers Trail through the Grand River Greenway is also expected to begin this year thanks to state support.

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the past 30 days (since ~July 18, 2026), plus a few critical items from earlier in 2026 that represent new developments not captured in the August 1 base research:

---

**Lake Sturgeon**

- 
A new study published around August 6, 2026 found that Great Lakes lake sturgeon can live up to 427 years, more than 275 years longer than previously thought.
 
The study, published in the *Journal of Fish Biology*, featured authors from the Michigan DNR, Michigan State University, Michigan Technological University, and the Wisconsin DNR.
 (Aug 6, 2026, WWMT/ClickOnDetroit)

- 
Funding for Grand River sturgeon research in 2026 is provided by the Great Lakes Fishery Trust.
 
A successful pilot hydroacoustic sampling study produced an annual spawner abundance estimate and a baseline of data for future management decisions, including images of sturgeon moving up the Grand River.
 (May 2026, Grand Rapids Public Museum)

**Snuffbox Mussel / Restoration Construction**

- 
On June 1, 2026, the City of Grand Rapids held a groundbreaking for the Grand River Restoration, Lower Reach project.
 
The city awarded a $14.56 million construction contract to Taplin Group LLC, with the work expected to improve habitat for lake sturgeon, river redhorse, and the federally endangered snuffbox mussel.
 (June 3, 2026, WWMT)

- 
As a requirement of the state permit, in-river construction cannot begin until July 1, 2026, to ensure water levels at the Sixth Street Dam continue to block invasive sea lamprey.
 
The 2026 project budget includes mussel relocation by BioSurvey Group and fish relocation by Encompass Socio-Ecological Consulting.
 (June 2026, Grand Rapids WhiteWater)

**Sea Lamprey / Sixth Street Dam**

- 
The Sixth Street Dam currently serves as a barrier preventing sea lamprey from accessing roughly 1,900 miles of upstream habitat, and it will not be removed until a new barrier is constructed, a project still being studied by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
 (July 15, 2026, Bridge Michigan)

- 
More than $2.1 million in EPA funding has been directed to the Great Lakes Fishery Commission for sea lamprey control on the Grand River, including designing a new state-of-the-art barrier and helping native fish species recover.
 
The barrier is expected to last 80 years and protect more than 4,000 miles of river; it will be installed after the rapids restoration project is complete.
 (WOOD TV8)

**Invasive Species**

entries.title: Hydrology and weather
entries.body:
Based on all searches, here is what is genuinely new or changed within roughly the last 30 days (since approximately July 18, 2026) for the Grand River Brain reference model. The major spring 2026 flood events are older than 30 days and already well-documented; the most relevant current-window findings are below:

---

- **No active flood warnings or advisories as of mid-August 2026.** 
No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for the Grand River at North Park Street, Grand Rapids
, per the NOAA National Water Prediction Service gauge page (NOAA NWPS, checked Aug 17, 2026).

- **Flow running below seasonal normal at Grand Rapids gauge (USGS 04119000), early-to-mid August 2026.** 
Grand River at Grand Rapids is flowing at approximately 2,280 cfs with the water sitting at 2.15 ft at the gauge, down 9% since the prior day as the gauge recedes.
 
Over the prior 10 days the average was 2,841 cfs, peaking at 3,180 cfs; the 5-day forecast projected continued recession toward roughly 2,092 cfs, running well below the seasonal normal.
 (Snoflo, referencing USGS gauge 04119000, early July 2026 forecast window)

- **Grand Rapids August precipitation tracking below normal month-to-date.** 
NWS Grand Rapids daily climate data show August month-to-date precipitation at 0.59 inches against a normal of 1.07 inches, a deficit of 0.48 inches; since June 1, precipitation totals 5.32 inches against a normal of 8.87 inches, a deficit of 3.55 inches.
 (NWS Grand Rapids Daily Climate, ~Aug 10, 2026)

- **NWS Grand Rapids 2026 National Hydrologic Assessment released.** 
The 2026 National Hydrologic Assessment has been released
, noted on the NOAA water prediction pages for the Grand Rapids forecast area (NOAA NWPS, July/August 2026).

- **NOAA flood inundation mapping now covers 60% of U.S. population,** including Grand Rapids area gauges. 
Flood Inundation Mapping services are now available for 60% of the U.S. population
, a capability expansion noted on the NWPS Grand Rapids gauge pages (NOAA NWPS, 2026).

entries.title: Construction progress
entries.body:
Now let me search for anything more recent (August 2026) to catch any updates in the last 30 days specifically.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since mid-July 2026), plus a few key items from July that may not yet be in the River Brain:

---

- **Lower Reach dam removal actively underway as of early August 2026:** 
As of August 3, 2026, crews are actively removing a dam just north of Gillett Bridge, one of four low-head dams being removed between I-196 and Fulton Street (WZZM13).


- **Taplin Group began in-river work July 1, 2026, starting with turbidity curtains and cofferdam:** 
In-river construction kicked off July 1 per state regulatory requirements; crews first installed turbidity curtains, then began scour protection around Gillette Bridge piers before installing a cofferdam to isolate a section for the first boulder arch structure (Spectrum News, July 2, 2026).


- **Ah-Nab-Awen Park closed for full two-year project duration, Gillett Bridge remains open:** 
Ah-Nab-Awen Park will remain closed throughout the construction period; Gillett Bridge will remain open (City of Grand Rapids PublicInput page, July 8, 2026).
 
The park closure also displaced the July 4 fireworks viewing area, with organizers moving the main viewing site away from Ah-Nab-Awen Park for the first time (HeyGrandRapids, June 30, 2026).


- **Upper Reach EIS public comment period closed May 22, 2026; draft EIS now expected July 2027:** 
The Great Lakes Fishery Commission and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers resumed the EIS process in spring 2026; the 30-day public comment period closed May 22, 2026, and a draft EIS is anticipated in July 2027 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater).


- **GLFC aquatic connectivity coordinator says Sixth Street Dam design selection not expected until 2028:** 
The Sixth Street Dam will not be removed until a new barrier is constructed, and GLFC aquatic connectivity coordinator Lisa Walter stated the project design selection is not expected until approximately 2028 (Bridge Michigan, July 15, 2026).


- **Over $20 million in federal funding committed for new lamprey barrier, proposed site is roughly one mile upstream of existing Sixth Street Dam:** 
More than $20 million in federal funding from the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative and the GLFC annual appropriation has been committed to the new lamprey barrier (Grand Rapids WhiteWater).
 
The new barrier is proposed to be located roughly one mile upstream from the existing Sixth Street Dam (Rep. Scholten press release).

Here are the genuinely new or changed items found from approximately the last 30 days (relative to Aug 10, 2026), plus a few closely relevant items from mid-2026 that post-date the August 1 base research date:

The Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians hosted their 44th annual Homecoming of the Three Fires on June 13–14, 2026 at Riverside Park in Grand Rapids, offering two days of traditional Native American culture and community gathering.
 (June 12, 2026, Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians website)

H.R. 3255, the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act of 2025, remains active in the 119th Congress. The Grand Rapids Public Museum's redesigned *Anishinabek: The People of This Place* exhibit, developed in collaboration with tribal leaders and the Eshtoojik Advisory Council, is set to reopen in Fall 2026. The updated exhibit will feature new technology, natural elements, connections to the Grand River, and art by local Anishinaabe artists.

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Now let me do a targeted search for the most recent (last 30 days, i.e., July 10 – August 10, 2026) Grand River news, and also for the Grand River Restoration construction update since it started July 1, 2026.
Here are the genuinely new or recently changed items relevant to the Grand River Brain, drawn from roughly the last 30 days (and a few closely preceding items that represent new developments not established in the August 1 baseline):

---

- **Grand River Restoration Lower Reach dam removal underway (July 1, 2026).** 
"Since construction began in early July, crews have already installed boulder drop structures by the Blue Bridge, near the Grand Rapids Public Museum."
 
The work is already producing visible results: "For the first time in 100 years, you can see whitewater, and you can actually hear rapids rushing through for quite a ways," said Matt Chapman of Grand Rapids WhiteWater.
 The approximately one-month-in progress report (WZZM13, ~Aug 2, 2026) is the most recent update on active construction.

- **Snuffbox mussel critical habitat expanded federally (April 24, 2026).** 
An action issued April 24 extended designated critical habitat range across 17 states, benefiting four species including the snuffbox (*Epioblasma triquetra*).
 
Mussel habitat designations in Michigan now explicitly include parts of the Grand River, Huron River, Flat River, and other named rivers, per the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
 (CBS Detroit, April 27, 2026)

- **2026 mussel relocation underway as condition of Grand River Restoration permit.** 
Construction cannot begin in the river until July 1, 2026, to protect fish spawning periods and maintain the Sixth Street Dam's sea lamprey barrier function; the project budget includes "2026 mussel relocation by BioSurvey Group" and "fish relocation by Encompass Socio-Ecological Consulting."
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater project page, updated June 2026)

- **New Michigan state-record gizzard shad caught in the Grand River, Kent County (April 22, 2026).** 
Sedrick Neinhuis, a Lowell angler, set a new Michigan state record catching a gizzard shad weighing 4.45 pounds and measuring 20.3 inches while spincasting on the Grand River in Kent County.
 
The catch surpasses the previous record of 4.12 pounds, set in 1996 on Lake St. Clair.
 (Michigan DNR, May 7, 2026)

- **Sea lamprey barrier design still unresolved for Sixth Street Dam replacement.** 
Starting July 1, Grand Rapids began removing four downtown dams, but officials are still studying how to remove a fifth dam (Sixth Street) and still keep out invasive sea lamprey.
 
The Great Lakes Fishery Commission has begun studying the environmental impacts of the proposed Upper Reach work, a process expected to take roughly two years before design work can begin.
 (Bridge Michigan, ~July 2026; Outdoor Hub, March 2026)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:

**July 22, 2026:** Gov. Whitmer signed Senate Bill 723 (Public Act 36 of 2026), revising the state's Transformational Brownfield Program by expanding oversight, tying tax reimbursements to measurable project performance, and raising the incentive capacity for future projects.
 
The law roughly doubles the program's annual capacity, authorizing an additional $80 million in state tax capture and raising the yearly ceiling to as much as $160 million, with the total aggregate cap rising to roughly $3.2 billion.
 
State officials cited stalled projects including riverfront work in Grand Rapids as examples of the capacity constraints the law is meant to relieve.

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from approximately the last 30 days (since ~July 3, 2026) and the most relevant recent developments since base research on August 1, 2026:

---

- **Grand River Restoration Lower Reach construction underway, July 1, 2026:** 
After 18 years of planning, crews entered the river July 1 to begin removing four low-head dams; the July 1 start date was set by state permit to ensure the Sixth Street Dam's water levels continue blocking invasive sea lamprey during construction.
 
Lower reach construction is expected to be completed by end of 2027.
 (Spectrum News / WWMT, July 2, 2026)

- **Snuffbox mussel relocation underway as part of dam removal, 2026:** 
The total project budget includes "2026 mussel relocation by BioSurvey Group" and fish relocation by Encompass Socio-Ecological Consulting
 as required conservation measures prior to and during construction. 
The Lower Reach will enhance aquatic habitat across 2,887 feet and 30 acres of river corridor, including improved habitat for lake sturgeon, river redhorse, and snuffbox mussel.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater / ExperienceGR, June–July 2026)

- **Sea lamprey 2026 control season active Great Lakes-wide, July 24, 2026:** 
Between April and November 2026, crews are applying lampricides TFM and Bayluscide to streams and still-water areas across the Great Lakes where young sea lamprey are present, with treatments highly effective at reducing larval numbers before they migrate.
 
This year's Canadian program covers tributaries on Lake Superior, Lake Huron, and Lake Ontario.
 (Sydenham Current / Great Lakes Commission, July 24, 2026)

- **Lake sturgeon research 2026 funded by Great Lakes Fishery Trust:** 
Funding for Grand River sturgeon research in 2026 is provided by the Great Lakes Fishery Trust, with the collaborative team including GRPM, John Ball Zoo, GVSU, Encompass Consulting, MDNR, and USFWS.
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum, 2026)

- **New Michigan state-record gizzard shad caught in Grand River, April 22, 2026:** 
An angler from Lowell, Michigan, caught a new state-record gizzard shad weighing 4.45 pounds and measuring 20.3 inches long, while spincasting on the Grand River in Kent County on April 22.
 
This beat the previous record of 4.12 pounds set in 1996 on Lake St. Clair.
 (Michigan DNR, May 7, 2026)

- **Invasive lesser celandine plant widely established in Grand River corridor:** 
According to the Michigan DNR, the invasive plant lesser celandine is already widely established along the Grand River corridor and is actively spreading in lower Michigan and southeastern Wisconsin.
 
Several partner organizations have formed the Michigan Lesser Celandine Coalition, recruiting volunteers to assess its spread

entries.title: Construction progress
entries.body:
Now let me do one more targeted search to check for any very recent news from the last 30 days (July 2026 to Aug 3, 2026) specifically.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (July 2026 through Aug 3, 2026), with notes where slightly older milestones from the research window are included because they represent state changes not previously captured in the River Brain base:

---

- **Lower Reach in-river construction started July 1, 2026.** 
The July 1 start date was set by state regulatory requirements to protect fish spawning periods and prevent sea lamprey from moving past the Sixth Street Dam; contractor Taplin Group opened by installing turbidity curtains in the river.
 
Over the following weeks, crews began building causeways for equipment access, and a cofferdam was installed to isolate a section of Dam 2 for the first boulder arch feature.
 (Spectrum News / City of Grand Rapids, July 1-2, 2026)

- **Ah-Nab-Awen Park confirmed closed for approximately two years.** 
Equipment staging began May 18, and the resulting Ah-Nab-Awen Park closure will continue through the full project period.
 
The park remains closed during this phase; the Gillett Bridge stays open.
 (City of Grand Rapids PublicInput, updated July 2026)

- **Active construction season runs July through mid-October or early November 2026.** 
Trucks and heavy equipment will be moving rocks and boulders in and out of the flowing river channel throughout the construction season, which runs roughly July through mid-October or early November each year, weather and river conditions permitting.
 Second construction season is anticipated for summer 2027. (Spectrum News, July 2, 2026)

- **Upper Reach EIS scoping comment period closed May 22, 2026; draft EIS now targeted for July 2027.** 
The EIS process, originally paused after 2019, was officially resumed by the Great Lakes Fishery Commission and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in spring 2026; a public scoping meeting was held April 22 and the 30-day comment period closed May 22; a draft EIS is anticipated in July 2027.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater, grandrapidswhitewater.org)

- **Army Corps of Engineers confirmed it is preparing the EIS for Sixth Street Dam removal and a replacement sea lamprey barrier.** 
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Detroit District is preparing an Environmental Impact Statement to evaluate removal of the 6th Street Dam and construction of a sea lamprey barrier on the Grand River in Grand Rapids.
 
Two barrier design alternatives are under consideration: a fixed crest design similar to the current dam, or an adjustable barrier dam.
 (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers / WZZM13, April 2026)

- **Over $20 million in federal funding committed to the new lamprey barrier for the Upper Reach.** 
More than $20 million in federal funding for a new lamprey barrier in the Grand River has been identified and committed to the Great Lakes Fishery Commission, sourced from Great Lakes Restoration Initiative funding and a GLFC annual budget appropriation.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater, grandrapidswhitewater.org)

entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently changed items relevant to the River Brain, all from within approximately the last 30 days or otherwise newly surfaced in 2026:

---

- **New book published, Jan. 13, 2026:** 
*The Historical Archaeology of Michigan* by Dean L. Anderson, Michael S. Nassaney, and Krysta Ryzewski was published by University Press of Florida on January 13, 2026 (280 pages).
 
The book covers the past 400 years of Michigan history through archaeological themes of entrepreneurship, immigration, capitalism, and civil rights, including chapters on European colonization, the fur trade, and 19th-century logging.
 (JSTOR / University Press of Florida)

- **Federal recognition bill reintroduced in House, May 8, 2025, Senate companion June 26, 2025:** 
U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) reintroduced the bipartisan Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act alongside Rep. John James (R-MI-10) on May 8, 2025.
 
Senators Elissa Slotkin and Gary Peters introduced companion Senate legislation on June 26, 2025.
 
The Grand River Bands are described as the last treaty tribe east of the Mississippi River without federal recognition.
 (Scholten House press release / Slotkin Senate press release)

- **H.R. 3255 in active 119th Congress:** 
The Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act of 2025 (H.R. 3255) formally affirms federal recognition of the tribe and makes members eligible for services and benefits provided to federally recognized tribes, regardless of reservation status.
 
The designated service area spans Newaygo, Oceana, Kent, Muskegon, and Ottawa Counties in Michigan.
 (Congress.gov)

- **GRPM "Ice Age: Michigan's Frozen Secrets" exhibit, open as of July 2026:** 
*Ice Age: Michigan's Frozen Secrets* and *Snow: Tiny Crystals, Global Impact* are now open at the Grand Rapids Public Museum.
 
The Ice Age exhibit explores North America during the last glacial period, featuring real Ice Age fossils including bones from the recently discovered "Clapp Family Mastodon."
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

- **GRPM Anishinaabe Star Knowledge planetarium show, active summer 2026:** 
The GRPM is currently featuring planetarium shows including *Anishinaabe Star Knowledge*, alongside *Secrets of the Sun* and *Dinosaurs: A Story of Survival*.
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

 Several of these (water hyacinth, water lettuce) are aquatic and relevant to Grand River watershed monitoring. (Michigan Invasive Species Program)
